title: Say it once: Introducing Bot Preference Sync
summary: Cloudflare's new Bot Preference Sync automatically aligns your robots.txt file with your AI bot policies for Search, Agent, and Training. Easily manage which bots access your content without maintaining static files.

title: How Ora benchmarks every major AI agent on Vercel
summary: Ora sends agents onto live websites with instructions to sign up for a product, integrate with it, and pay for it. Agents often fail, and by Ora's estimate, 99% of the web isn't agent-ready. The platform shows customers where and why agents fail, and what to change.

title: A Tale of Two Flink Autoscalers
summary: Today, Netflix runs two Flink autoscalers. That is exactly one more than we want. We built the first one in-house years ago, when there was no mature option suited to our platform. The second came from the Apache Flink community, and it can scale workloads our homegrown system was never designed for. We now run both…

title: Total eclipse of the Internet: traffic impacts in Iceland, Spain, and Portugal
summary: Cloudflare's data shows a clear impact on Internet traffic from Iceland to Spain and Portugal, following the path of totality of the total solar eclipse that occurred on August 12, 2026.

title: Inside the Vercel intern experience
summary: The best way to learn is by shipping product to users in production, and that's why we don’t treat our interns as temporary guests. Every intern at Vercel is expected to operate like a core part of our engineering team from day one.

title: Building a software factory for AI SDK
summary: The AI SDK is one of the most popular open-source AI projects in the world. It serves over 20 million npm downloads a week and the repo has over 26,000 stars. Maintaining the codebase means tracking four moving targets at once:

title: From all-or-nothing to task-based OAuth consent
summary: Cloudflare OAuth now supports optional scopes, giving users more control over what an app can access and helping developers build secure consent flows around the task at hand.

title: How v0 authenticates to Snowflake without exposing the user's OAuth token
summary: AI-generated applications often need to authenticate to external services on behalf of their users. That creates a problem: generated code shouldn't have access to the user's credentials.

title: Improving infrastructure efficiency for growing demand in the age of AI
summary: As demand for AI continues to grow, so does the infrastructure needed to support it.

title: BGP Role model: tracking the adoption of RFC 9234
summary: RFC 9234 lets routers reject route leaks on their own, using BGP Roles and the Only to Customer attribute. We measured who has deployed it, and found two Tier 1 networks unexpectedly stripping OTC.

title: When Can LLMs Replace Humans in A/B Tests?
summary: TL;DR: LLM predictions can stand in for human outcomes in A/B tests, but only by assumption, not by design....

title: Certificate Transparency Monitoring is now generally available
summary: Cloudflare's Certificate Transparency Monitoring is now generally available. The biggest change: we no longer email you about certificates Cloudflare issued for your domain, so when an alert lands in your inbox, it's worth a look.

title: Project HydraFusion: Frontier quality via multi-model orchestration
summary: In controlled offline evaluations, HydraFusion’s selective coding workflows matched or exceeded the evaluated Opus 5 baseline while reducing estimated workflow cost. Now available as a research preview in GitHub Copilot.

title: MAPS: Netflix’s Multimodal Asset Personalization at Scale
summary: By Emma Yanyang Kong , Aditya Deshpande , Asad Abbasi , Bowei Yan , David Fagnan , Ashish Rastogi , Dhaval Patel , Ray Zhang

title: BotBase for Operators: A clearer path to joining Cloudflare's directory of bots and agents
summary: Bot operators now have a home in the Cloudflare dashboard to manage submissions. This update adds submission status tracking, submission editing, and a behavior model so operators can accurately declare how their bots use content.

title: The best workflow engine is a programming language
summary: The idea of orchestrating long-running, stateful logic on top of unreliable, stateless infrastructure isn't new. We've had message queues, job runners, microservice choreographies, and full-blown workflow engines for a long time. What we never had was a version of it that felt good to write.

title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: Managing your work
summary: If you’re juggling multiple Copilot sessions, use the My work pane to track what's in flight, what's done, and what's next.

title: Introducing Vercel for Slack
summary: Vercel Agent now works in Slack. Mention it the way you'd pull a teammate into a thread, and it reads the discussion, answers with the context of the platform running your app, and turns the team's decisions into changes you approve. Vercel for Slack is available today in Public Beta for Pro and Enterprise teams.

title: Introducing context-aware vulnerability discovery and remediation with Cloudflare Managed Defense and OpenAI Daybreak models
summary: Use production traffic and security signals to prioritize findings, prepare edge mitigations when safe, and propose code patches. By combining WAF data with OpenAI Daybreak models, Vulnerability Discovery and Remediation helps teams identify and patch the most critical threats first.

title: Portal by Spotify cut my Claude Code token usage by 90%
summary: Most of what an AI coding agent does for me isn't thinking. It's I/O.

title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: Run several agents at once
summary: Learn how to run parallel agents in the GitHub Copilot app, and experience the moment it stops feeling scary and starts feeling powerful.

title: How we saved 100 terabytes of memory by optimizing 1.1.1.1’s DNS cache
summary: Five Rust-level memory optimizations to the DNS cache layout of Big Pineapple cut per-entry memory by 56%, freeing approximately 100 TB of memory across Cloudflare's fleet.

title: GitHub Copilot app for Beginners: Automate Dependabot pull request triage
summary: Managing library updates can be tedious at times. Learn how the GitHub Copilot app can handle this type of repetitive task.

title: A revisit of remote Spectre attacks on Cloudflare Workers
summary: In 2024 and 2025, we reassessed remote Spectre attacks on our Workers infrastructure. We share details about the new attack primitives like Spectre gadgets, remote timers, achieving co-location and how new defenses further harden Cloudflare Workers.

title: Decoding the new AI lingo: Loops, harnesses, squads, hill climbing… oh my!
summary: From loop engineering to harnesses, squads, and open weights, the GitHub Podcast breaks down the AI terms showing up in developer conversations.

title: How we make AI coding more cost efficient without sacrificing task quality
summary: Why shorter outputs can cost more, and how GitHub Copilot reduces wasted work across the complete coding task.

title: How to evaluate LLMs before production
summary: These are the lessons we learned evaluating LLMs for real-world secret scanning.

title: Introducing Run SDK: secure eval for your agents
summary: Agents increasingly write TypeScript programs to coordinate tools and process their results. Once those programs touch real applications, some steps require authentication, while others need human approval.

title: The end of credential sprawl for agents
summary: Every useful agent reaches beyond your codebase. It posts to Slack, opens pull requests, queries Snowflake, or calls an internal API. That reach is what makes it valuable, and it's also where the risk lives, because for years, granting it meant provisioning a long-lived token and hoping it never leaked.

title: $1 million hacker challenge for Vercel Sandbox
summary: Agents need to run untrusted code, and the microVM has become the standard way to do it: a dedicated guest kernel per workload, isolated from the host and from every other workload on the same machine.

title: How we could save petabytes of cache storage with Zstandard and Pingora
summary: Could we get more cache space with the same hardware? We prototyped compression inside Cloudflare's cache to find out.

title: Compute that takes any shape
summary: Workloads differ in how long they run, how much memory they take, and how much of the environment they control. That previously meant a different compute primitive for each job, so product iterations required provisioning infrastructure, not just working on a feature.

title: Your alt text passes automated checks. That doesn’t mean it’s any good.
summary: We built a plugin for the GitHub Accessibility Scanner to make sure your alt text is actually accessible. Here's how it works.

title: The Cloudflare Blog — brought to you by EmDash
summary: We migrated the Cloudflare Blog to EmDash to prove our stack at massive scale. Here is how we stress-tested performance, safely routed production traffic, and redesigned the frontend experience.

title: Intent to Ship: JPEG XL
summary: It isn’t often that new image formats land in browsers. In the early 2000s we had JPEG, GIF, and PNG. The 2010s gave us WebP, which was a modest step up from JPEG. But the 2020s have given us two new image formats that are a big step up from previous formats: AVIF and JPEG

title: Everything we launched during Agents Week
summary: Our latest Agents Week has come to a close. Here’s a recap of all the announcements we made from Wallets to Radar.

title: Rerouting the Stream: How Lyft Moved to the Apache Flink Operator
summary: Written by Maheep Myneni , Arda Kuyumcu , and Prem Santosh Udaya Shankar at Lyft.

title: Testing cookie behavior across hundreds of web surfaces with our in-house auditor
summary: Our cookie auditor acts like a privacy-conscious user by visiting web pages and checking that they only load cookies consistent with that user’s preferences.

title: How our agents build on-brand pages with design.md
summary: Across Vercel, we use coding agents to design and build pages that have to look and feel like Vercel. The typography, color, and composition all need to carry the same judgment that we put into the pages we already ship ourselves.

title: Serving the most critical missions: Cloudflare for Government achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) Certified status
summary: Cloudflare for Government achieves FedRAMP Class D (High) Certified status. We also announce our commitment to pursue DoD IL4 authorization. Cloudflare brings world-class security, performance, and developer products to the public sector.
